description: The Water Distribution System Research Database grew out of the ASCE Task Committee on Research Databases for Water Distribution Systems, formed in 2013 to give the water distribution community a database for developing and testing algorithms for network design, analysis and operations. Volunteers collected data files and narratives for more than 40 distribution systems, from networks well known in the literature such as the New York Tunnel System to systems known only to the contributor; each entry includes an EPANET-compatible file and a summary of the system's history and characteristics. The UKnowledge site groups them into historic literature systems, software manual examples, Battle of the Water Network models, the Kentucky and Kentucky valved datasets, US, international and synthetic systems, and the database has its own DOI. Coverage is the collected networks. Access is free as EPANET input files on the university repository. Caveats: no licence is stated on the home page, and the entries were contributed by volunteers. Simulation uses: hydraulic and resilience analysis, design optimisation and sensor placement on shared benchmark networks. Related records: BattLeDIM (data-battledim-leakage-detection-benchmark), the DHALSIM C-Town and Anytown datasets (data-dhalsim-ctown-anytown-cyber-physical-datasets) and EPANET (model-epanet).
